items.title: [Bug]: Evaluation job reports RESULTS_UPLOADED with empty results when every validate task aborts
items.body:
Closes #754.

## Problem

Both evaluation controllers fire `VALIDATION_RESULT_RECEIVED` **before** they inspect the result's
return code — stock `CrossSiteModelEval._accept_val_result` at `cross_site_model_eval.py:416-423`, and
FLIP's own `ModelEval` at `fed_evaluation.py:232-236`. An aborted `validate` task therefore reached
`EvaluationJsonGenerator` carrying no DXO at all. `from_shareable()` raised on it, the exception was
logged and discarded, and nothing recorded that a task had failed.

`ServerEventHandler` then decided the terminal status from only two signals — `fatal_error`
(`FATAL_SYSTEM_ERROR`) and `STOPPED` (`FlipEvents.ABORTED`). `TASK_ABORTED` is neither, so a run in
which *every* task failed fell through to `RESULTS_UPLOADED`: indistinguishable from success in the API
and the UI, with an empty `evaluation_results.json` and the only evidence buried in `error_log.txt`
inside the zip.

This is why the failure was eval-specific: `ScatterAndGather` `system_panic`s on any non-OK result, so
training runs already surface `ERROR`. `GlobalModelEval` merely logs "Logging empty results" and carries on.

## Changes

**Record the failures.** `EvaluationJsonGenerator` now reads the return code *before* attempting the DXO
conversion and records each failed task as `{model, client, return_code}`, written to a new
`evaluation_results/evaluation_failures.json`. The file is always written, so an empty `[]` positively
means "no task failed" rather than "this version didn't record them". A reply that arrives with `rc == OK`
but the wrong data kind counts as a failure too — otherwise an evaluation where every client returned
garbage would still report success.

**Fail the run.** `ServerEventHandler` reports `ERROR` when the evaluation produced failures and no
results at all. Results are still uploaded either way — the zip is what carries `evaluation_failures.json`
and `error_log.txt`.

Terminal-status precedence is consolidated into a single `_terminal_status` helper, most salient cause
first:

```
fatal system error  >  user abort  >  every validate task failed  >  upload outcome
```

A user-requested stop aborts every in-flight `validate` task, so `STOPPED` **must** outrank the failures
it necessarily caused — otherwise stopping an evaluation would be reported as a crash. Training jobs wire
the base `ValidationJsonGenerator`, which tracks no failures, so they are excluded by construction rather
than by a flag.

**Fix a latent bug the incident masked.** `GlobalModelEval` sends one `validate` task per (model, client)
and sets `MODEL_OWNER`, but results were keyed by client alone — so each model's metrics silently
overwrote the previous model's, and a two-model evaluation only ever reported its *last* model. Results
now nest under the model name when the controller supplies one. The legacy `ModelEval` controller sets no
`MODEL_OWNER` (it sends every model in one task, and the evaluator returns its own model-keyed dict), so
that job type keeps its existing flat shape.

> **Breaking output change.** `evaluation_results.json` for `evaluation_client_api` nests one level
> deeper: `{"<trust>": {"SRV_<model>": {...}}}` instead of `{"<trust>": {...}}`. Documented in the two
> app READMEs and the Ark+ guide.

## Verification

Driven through the real `FlipEvalRecipe` on the NVFLARE simulator (`SimEnv`, 2 models × 2 clients — the
topology of the production incident), with an `origin/develop` baseline run for comparison.

| Scenario | `develop` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Every `validate` task aborts | `RESULTS_UPLOADED`, `{}`, 8 swallowed `not a valid DXO` tracebacks | `ERROR`, 4 failures recorded, **0** tracebacks |
| Clean 2-model run | `{"site-1": {"weight_sum": 10.0}}` — one model's metrics lost | `{"site-1": {"SRV_arkplus_pretrained": {...}, "SRV_arkplus_finetuned": {...}}}` |
| Partial failure | — | `RESULTS_UPLOADED`, successful metrics uploaded, failures recorded |
| Clean run | — | `evaluation_failures.json == []` |

Both artefacts are written inside the uploaded run directory, so they reach the results zip. Also confirmed
that all four training app configs and `FlipFedAvgRecipe` wire the base `ValidationJsonGenerator`, so the
`isinstance` guard correctly excludes training jobs.

`503` unit tests pass; `ruff` clean.

### Stag verification (2026-07-10)

Deployed `flare-fl-server:8f8389f65eb…` (this branch's head) onto the staging hub's `fl-server-net-1`
and ran the Ark+ **multimodel** evaluation (`evaluation_client_api`, 2 models × 2 trusts — the
production incident's exact topology) end-to-end via `tests/e2e_smoke.py` against
`stag.flip.aicentre.co.uk`, with the GSTT/KCH trusts on a GPU desktop and the DeCaf holdout cohorts
(478/468 studies):

- **All-failed path (organic):** the first run's `validate` tasks all aborted client-side (the
  tutorial's evaluator needs the FLIP-Ark fork's named-broadcast meta, which upstream `flip` doesn't
  ship yet — a tutorial↔platform version gap, unrelated to this fix). The branch behaved exactly as
  designed: model ended **`ERROR`** (develop would have reported `RESULTS_UPLOADED`), the zip still
  uploaded, `evaluation_results.json == {}`, and `evaluation_failures.json` recorded all 4
  `(model, client, TASK_ABORTED)` tuples. No swallowed `from_shareable` tracebacks.
- **Clean path:** with the evaluator shimmed to infer the model from the state-dict head signature,
  the run ended **`RESULTS_UPLOADED`** with `evaluation_failures.json == []` and the nested results
  shape carrying **both** models per trust — `{"Trust_N": {"SRV_arkplus_pretrained": {…},
  "SRV_arkplus_finetuned": {…}}}`. The pretrained AUROCs reproduce the baseline table in
  `ARKPLUS_EXPERIMENTS_GUIDE.md` (GSTT: Effusion 0.839, Consolidation 0.866, Infiltration 0.845,
  Nodule/Mass 0.944, Pneumothorax 0.643; KCH matches likewise) — metrics the pre-fix keying would
  have silently overwritten for one of the two models.

The staging fl-server was restored to its previous pinned image after verification.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] An evaluation run in which **every** `validate` task fails ends in a failure status surfaced via the
      API and UI (`ERROR`), not `RESULTS_UPLOADED`.
- [x] `EvaluationJsonGenerator` checks the peer return code before attempting DXO conversion and records
      per-task failures (model + client + rc) instead of raising and discarding them.
- [x] Partial failures still upload the successful results, with the failure set recorded in the results
      bundle (`evaluation_failures.json`), so a partially failed evaluation is detectable without reading
      `error_log.txt`.
- [x] Unit tests cover: all-tasks-aborted → failure status; partial-abort → failures recorded alongside
      results.

## Out of scope

While tracing this I found that `ClientExceptionReporter` is dead code for **both Client-API job types**,
and that a bad import in a user's evaluator hangs the job indefinitely. Neither is fixed here — filed as
#755, with the design options written up.


## Acceptance Criteria

*Imported from issue #754*

- [x] An evaluation run in which **every** `validate` task fails (rc set / aborted) ends in a failure status surfaced via the API and UI (e.g. `ERROR`), not `RESULTS_UPLOADED`.
- [x] `EvaluationJsonGenerator` checks the peer return code before attempting DXO conversion and records per-task failures (model + client + rc) instead of raising and discarding them.
- [x] Partial failures (some clients/models succeeded) still upload the successful results but the failure set is recorded in the results bundle (e.g. in `run_metadata`/results JSON), so a partially failed evaluation is detectable without reading `error_log.txt`.
- [x] Unit tests cover: all-tasks-aborted → failure status; partial-abort → failures recorded alongside results.

## Root cause

The rescue query builder generated useful Occu-Med buyer-language aliases, but the browser rescue executes only the first four queries. Those first four were all literal/operator variations of the user's wording, so aliases such as occupational health, employee health, pre-employment physicals, and fitness-for-duty never ran. - Recognize broad medical-employment wording as an Occu-Med service intent while keeping non-medical HR/performance wording out of that override.
- Wire the search route to `applyOccuMedSmartFilter`.

items.title: fix(evaluation): Bug B — bound regex-fallback summary capture (over-capture)
items.body:
Completes the Bug B arc (capture instrumentation #120 → DB/UI observability #122 → **this fix**). Standalone precursor ahead of the v2.13.2 visitor decomposition; does not touch scoring or the prompt.

## The bug

When strict JSON parse fails, `ClaudeEvaluationStrategy.parseEvaluation` falls back to regex extraction whose summary pattern was greedy:

```
SUMMARY_PATTERN = (?s)"summary"\s*:\s*"(.*)"\s*[,}]
```

The greedy `.*` captured to the **last** quote before `,`/`}`, over-capturing the following field into the summary — observed in the cache as `"summary":"…horizon.','headline"}"`. The rating was always safe (extracted by an independent integer pattern); only the summary was cosmetically mangled.

## The fix (fallback summary/basic_summary only)

`SUMMARY_PATTERN` / `BASIC_SUMMARY_PATTERN` are now **bounded**:

```
"summary"\s*:\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*[,}]
```

`(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*` matches any run of non-quote / escaped characters and stops at the first **genuine (unescaped)** closing quote — so it physically cannot swallow `","headline":"..."`. Embedded `\"` escapes are handled without truncating early.

## One deliberate departure from "bounded alone" — for rating safety

**Bounded-alone would *regress* rating safety.** A summary with *internal* unescaped quotes (the existing `"orange"` fallback test) yields **no bounded match** → `summaryMatcher.find()` is false → the whole fallback **throws**, losing the rating too. That's worse than the benign bug.

So I used **bounded-first, greedy-salvage** (`extractField`): bounded kills the common over-capture (well-formed summary + malformed *following* field — the observed artifact), and the legacy greedy pattern only salvages when bounded can't match (internal-quote summaries), preserving the rating. Net:

- Over-capture **fixed** for the observed class.
- **Rating safety preserved** — never throws away a rating the old code salvaged.
- **Existing 40 `ClaudeEvaluationStrategy` tests pass unchanged** — the `"orange"` case now routes through the greedy salvage. (Bounded-alone would have broken this.)

## Not touched

`RATING_PATTERN`, rating extraction, `RatingValidator`, `RatingCombiner`, `SkyVisitor`, scoring, the strict-parse happy path, the prompt. `HEADLINE_PATTERN` / `BLUEBELL_SUMMARY_PATTERN` use `[^"]+` (already bounded, no over-capture) — left as-is.

## Synthetic fixture (why)

The over-capture is a **silent success**, so the real malformed `rawText` was never persisted, and it's rare (733 consecutive batch responses parsed strictly, zero fallbacks). The fix is correct against the entire over-capture **class**, not one instance, so a clearly-labelled synthetic fixture (reconstructing the real Angel-of-the-North cache artifact) is used and **not** presented as a captured production response. The live capture instrumentation from #122 remains the post-hoc real-data check.

## Tests (47, all green)

Over-capture summary stays clean; clean summary + well-formed headline both extract; escaped-quote boundary preserved; `basic_summary` bounded; happy-path strict parse unchanged; existing fallback/`"orange"` test unchanged. Checkstyle + spotbugs clean; parser consumers + prompt golden masters green.

## Post-deploy check (occasional, manual)

```sql
SELECT region_name, evaluation_date, target_type FROM cached_evaluation
WHERE source='BATCH' AND evaluation_date >= CURRENT_DATE
  AND (results_json LIKE '%''headline%' OR results_json LIKE '%'',''%');
-- expect zero rows over time
```

items.title: Analytical Dynamics: double-pendulum derivation, bug fixes, and n-link generalization (n=3, n=5)
items.body:
## Summary

- Got the `AnalyticalDynamics` double-pendulum code actually running for the first time (submodules weren't checked out, scientific packages weren't installed) and re-derived its equations of motion by hand from the Lagrangian.
- Found and fixed a real bug: the θ₂'' formula had a term coded as a sum where the derivation requires a product. Verified via energy conservation — drift dropped from ~150 J (100,000% of E₀) to ~6×10⁻⁶ J (0.004%).
- Added a from-scratch **symbolic** (SymPy) Lagrangian derivation, generalized to an arbitrary planar n-link pendulum chain. Validated: n=1 reduces to the simple pendulum; n=2 matches the hand-derived, bug-fixed code to 8.9×10⁻¹⁵ over 200 random states; n=3–5 conserve energy to within integrator error.
- Rendered chaotic-regime GIF animations for n=3 and n=5 from the validated symbolic model, and extended the fuzzy TSK surrogate-modeling study from n=2 to n=3/n=5.
- **Found and fixed two bugs** in how the *original* n=2 study measured iterative-rollout accuracy (seeded with the whole true trajectory instead of the initial condition, and a stale-row slice for `window_size>1`) — patched directly in `test_double_pendulum.py`.
- **A full rollout-stability investigation** on n=2 and n=3, culminating in physics-inspired consequent equations (basis features derived from the true equations of motion via Cramer's rule on the symbolic manipulator equation, dividing by the exact known denominator instead of learning it) — and a self-correction of that investigation's own black-box comparison baseline:

  | Approach | n | Time to 0.5 rad error |
  |---|---|---|
  | Angle-only inputs | 2 | 0.32–0.45s (insensitive to tuning) |
  | Angle + velocity, `n_output_buckets=3` (as first reported) | 2 | 0.60s |
  | Angle + velocity, tuned (`n_output_buckets≈10`) | 2 | ~1.15s |
  | Physics-informed consequent, genuine fuzzy TSK (`n_output_buckets=40`) | 2 | 2.47s |
  | Physics-informed consequent, plain linear regression | 2 | **3.31s** |
  | Angle-only baseline (fan config), any bucket count | 3 | ~0.48s (insensitive to tuning) |
  | Physics-informed consequent, genuine fuzzy TSK (`n_output_buckets=40`) | 3 | 2.26s |
  | Physics-informed consequent, plain linear regression | 3 | **3.98s** |

  Initially reported the n=2 physics-informed result as a >5× win over black-box; digging into *why* the fuzzy library did poorly on the physics-basis features (it wasn't the "clustering instability" first guessed — `n_output_buckets` partitions by *output value*, and low counts bias each local fit) led to checking whether the black-box baselines were themselves under-tuned. They were, partially: angle+velocity nearly doubles with more fuzzy rules, shrinking n=2's multiplier to a fair **~2–3×**; n=3's baseline is missing velocity information no bucket count can supply, so its **~5–8×** multiplier holds. Corrected in place in the report rather than left standing — same self-audit standard this PR has applied throughout (§2's bug fix, §4's rollout-evaluation bugs).

## Reports

- `AnalyticalDynamics/DOUBLE_PENDULUM_REPORT.md` — derivation, state-space expansion, the α₂ bug/fix, chaos characterization, and an in-place correction of the original rollout claim.
- `AnalyticalDynamics/N_PENDULUM_SYMBOLIC_DERIVATION.md` — the symbolic n-link generalization and its validation.
- `AnalyticalDynamics/N3_N5_FUZZY_REGRESSION_REPORT.md` — the n=3/n=5 surrogate study, all rollout-evaluation bugs, the full rollout-stability investigation (§4.1–4.6), and the bucket-count tuning correction (§4.7).

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest AnalyticalDynamics/test_double_pendulum.py` passes end-to-end against the corrected physics **and** the patched rollout evaluation.
- [x] `python AnalyticalDynamics/double_pendulum_classical_dynamics.py`, `n_pendulum_validation.py`, `n_pendulum_animation.py` — physics validation and GIFs.
- [x] `python AnalyticalDynamics/n_pendulum_fuzzy_regression.py`, `n_pendulum_regression_comparison.py`, `n_pendulum_velocity_ablation.py`, `n2_moving_average_fuzzy.py`, `n2_energy_conserving_fuzzy.py` — the rollout-stability ablation series.
- [x] `python AnalyticalDynamics/n2_physics_informed_fuzzy.py`, `n2_physics_informed_v2_rational.py`, `n3_physics_informed_rational.py` — physics-informed consequent equations, n=2 and n=3.
- [x] `python AnalyticalDynamics/n_output_bucket_sensitivity.py` — the bucket-count tuning check and correction.

Still queued (not in this PR): full chaos/Lyapunov results sections for n=3/n=5 as standalone topics, and extending the physics-informed consequent approach to n=5.

The backend's `POST /api/traces/search` response, in digest mode, already attaches `evaluations` per trace (`app.v1.ts`, via `enrichTracesWithEvaluations`) — but `mcp-server`'s `TraceSearchResult` type never declared that field, and `search_traces`'s digest formatter silently dropped it. `get_trace` (single trace) already surfaced evaluations correctly; `search_traces` (the list view an agent actually uses to scan many traces) did not — forcing N `get_trace` calls to check eval status across N traces instead of one `search_traces` call. items.title: cor-759 - AQL unary plus/minus on bind parameters silently return incorrect values
items.body:
This PR resolves below mentioned two Issues.
**Original Issues:** 
https://github.com/arangodb/arangodb/issues/22907 
https://github.com/arangodb/arangodb/issues/22908

Unary operators with bind parameters in AQL queries are not producing the expected results.

**Steps to reproduce:**
Run AQL Query:

```js
db._query(
  `RETURN {
    directPlus: +@x,
    directMinus: -@x,
    doubleMinus: -(-@x),
    viaSubtraction: 0 - @x,
    absDirectMinus: ABS(-@x),
    absSubtraction: ABS(0 - @x)
   
  }`,
  {
    x: 1
  }
).toArray();
```
db._query(  `RETURN -(-(-@x))`,  {    x: 1  }).toArray();

**Root cause:** parse-time unary optimization treats bind parameters as constant and calls castToNumber() before they're substituted. The crash is a parse-time assertion failure, not a runtime evaluation bug.

**Fix applied**
In Ast::optimizeUnaryOperatorArithmetic(), skip folding unless the operand is already a VALUE / ARRAY / OBJECT. Bind-parameter (and similar) nodes are left for later AST optimization after injection.

**After Fix:**
```js
127.0.0.1:8529@_system> db._query(  `RETURN {    directPlus: +@x,    directMinus: -@x,    doubleMinus: -(-@x),    viaSubtraction: 0 - @x,    absDirectMinus: ABS(-@x),    absSubtraction: ABS(0 - @x),    nooptMinus: -NOOPT(@x)  }`,  {    x: 1  }).toArray();
[ 
  { 
    "directPlus" : 1, 
    "directMinus" : -1, 
    "doubleMinus" : 1, 
    "viaSubtraction" : -1, 
    "absDirectMinus" : 1, 
    "absSubtraction" : 1, 
    "nooptMinus" : -1 
  } 
]

127.0.0.1:8529@_system> db._query(  `RETURN -(-(-@x))`,  {    x: 1  }).toArray();
[
  -1
]
```

The live harness only ever fetched `verdict.json`. It never captured usage, so **every live run scored `cost=0`** and the aggregate reported `$0.00/case` — a cost comparison that silently claims "free". That is worse than reporting nothing, because it looks like an answer.

It also had a concrete consequence: the #120 slice-1 measurements could not use `scripts/run-eval-live.sh` at all, and had to be driven through the in-app eval instead.

## The fix

The runner now also calls **`GET /api/sessions/:id/usage`** (new, read-only) and writes `meta.json` — which `run-eval.js` already knew how to merge into a case result. Usage is computed server-side by the **same `sumUsage`** the in-app runner uses, extracted to `lib/session-usage.js` so there is one definition rather than two that can drift, and it carries the #120 delegation breakdown. A live run and an in-app run now report the same measurement under the same keys.

Ordering is safe by construction: the turn's final usage (and the whole-turn cost) is pushed before the session stops reporting `running`, which is what the runner's wait loop keys off.

## Three things this turned up

**A case that spent money but produced no verdict was dropped entirely** — `readResult` returned `null`, so it scored as `cost 0`. The most wasteful possible outcome (an expensive investigation that concluded nothing) was the cheapest line in the report. It now scores `inconclusive`, which is what a missing verdict means, while keeping its real cost. The "no verdict" warning is keyed off the verdict file so it still fires for exactly the cases it always did.

**`run-eval.js` called `main()` on import**, so none of it could be unit-tested. Added the standard entry-point guard, and verified the CLI still runs end-to-end (offline mode, real cases, cost picked up from `meta.json`) rather than trusting the guard.

**The 3s poll interval is now injectable** — the new runner tests went from 24s to 0.3s.

## Stale comment corrected

The header said *"Until (1) lands, prefer the offline `--results` path"* while listing (1) as already IMPLEMENTED four lines above. All three prerequisites are satisfied by the eval compose profile that `run-eval-live.sh` brings up; what remains true is that this path needs a live appliance and so is still unexercised in CI.

## Risk

Low. The new route is read-only and derives from the transcript. Nothing in the write path, credentials or agent loop is touched. The one behaviour change outside the harness is `readResult` returning a result for a verdict-less case — covered by tests, and it can only *add* cost that was previously discarded, never change a disposition.

Worth naming: this makes live-run costs **appear** where they previously read as $0, so historical live runs in `history.jsonl` are not comparable to new ones on cost. In-app runs are unaffected and remain comparable.

## Validation

- `npm run check` ✅ `bash scripts/lint.sh` ✅ `bash eval/dashboard/ci.sh` — gate PASS ✅
- `npm test` — **702 pass** (was 690) ✅ `npm run smoke` — **81 pass** ✅
- New tests: the usage route (including that an unknown session 404s rather than answering "zero cost"), the runner's capture against a stub app speaking the real endpoints (verdict + meta, exact scorer key names, usage-endpoint failure, and the spent-but-no-verdict case), and `readResult` assembly.
- CLI verified by hand after the entry-point guard: `node eval/harness/run-eval.js --results … --reports …` still scores and writes, picking up `cost_usd` from `meta.json`.

items.title: chore(evaluation): Bug B capture instrumentation (v2.13.2 precursor)
items.body:
## What

Adds a single diagnostic `WARN` log in `ClaudeEvaluationStrategy.parseEvaluation` at the point the regex fallback is invoked (i.e. whenever strict JSON parsing of a Claude response fails), logging the raw response truncated to 4000 chars.

This is a **precursor-to-the-precursor** for the v2.13.2 work: it exists only to recover a real malformed Claude response from production, so the actual Bug B fix can be written and regression-tested against a real fixture rather than a guessed one.

## Why

"Bug B" is the over-capture defect: when Claude returns malformed JSON, the greedy regex fallback (`SUMMARY_PATTERN`'s `.*`) swallows adjacent fields — e.g. the `headline` key — into the `summary` string. It was observed in the live cache as `"summary":"…horizon.','headline"}`.

The problem with fixing it is **the real raw input is captured nowhere**:

- The over-capture case is a **silent success** — strict parse fails, the regex fallback *succeeds*, and `parseEvaluation` returns a valid result (`succeeded=true`).
- `JobRunService.logBatchResult` never sets `response_body`, so it is `null` for every batch row (success *and* error).
- The existing raw-text `LOG.warn` fires only when the fallback *also* fails (a true `parse_error`), not for over-capture.

So only the mangled **output** survives (in `cached_evaluation`), never the input. Per the investigation's discipline ("don't invent the fixture; capture a real one"), this instrumentation makes the otherwise-invisible fallback invocations — including over-capture successes — emit their raw input to the rolling log.

## Scope / safety

- **Logging only — parsing behaviour is unchanged.** The 40 existing `ClaudeEvaluationStrategyTest` cases pass untouched.
- Does **not** alter `RATING_PATTERN`, `RatingValidator`, `RatingCombiner`, the strict-parse happy path, the prompt, or any scoring/visitor code.
- New `ClaudeEvaluationStrategyCaptureTest` (4 tests): proves the capture fires on the fallback path, stays silent on the happy path, leaves parse results unchanged, and bounds over-long raw text. No `@SpringBootTest`, no `lenient()`, no `any()` in verify.
- Checkstyle clean.

## Next steps (not in this PR)

1. Deploy this.
2. After a nightly cycle with a recurrence, on the host:
   `grep "Bug B capture" /Users/gregochr/goldenhour-data/logs/goldenhour.log*`
   and capture a real malformed `rawText` (ideally an over-capture case whose cache summary shows the `','headline` artifact).
3. Use that real fixture to implement + regression-test the fallback hardening (bounded non-greedy summary/headline capture, or repair-and-reparse) on a separate `fix/bug-b-summary-overcapture` branch.

items.title: refactor(evals): put results/ under a schema and drift gate (#926)
items.body:
## Summary

Puts `evals/*/results/` under a schema and a drift gate, and migrates every
committed run record onto it. `results/` was this repository's only committed
machine-readable corpus with no schema and no gate, and it drifted anyway --
which is the finding worth carrying beyond this directory: choosing JSON is
not what prevents drift, a schema plus a gate is.

## Facts

Measured at `edd14f4`, re-confirmed byte-identical at `4c17391`, against the
ten keys `evals/evaluating-skill-quality/results/README.md` declares as its
own manifest minimum:

| Run | Keys | Layout violations |
|---|---|---|
| `battle-testing-a-skill/2026-07-30-issue-584-dispatch-trace` | 10/10 | no `artifacts[]` |
| `evaluating-skill-quality/2026-07-28-issue-500-phase1` | 10/10 | no `artifacts[]` |
| `evaluating-skill-quality/2026-07-30-issue-584-dispatch-trace` | 10/10 | no `artifacts[]` |
| `evaluating-skill-quality/2026-07-29-issue-537-confidentiality-gates` | 7/10 | `model` (singular) |
| `untrusted-input-triage/2026-08-01-issue-645-battle-test` | 7/10 | 3 unreferenced `.md` in root |
| `untrusted-input-triage/2026-08-01-issue-645-behavioral-eval` | 7/10 | 4 unreferenced `.md` in root |
| `untrusted-input-triage/2026-08-01-issue-646-behavioral-gate2` | 3/10 | 5 unreferenced `.md` in root |
| `untrusted-input-triage/2026-08-01-issue-646-transfer-check` | no manifest | 1 unreferenced `.md` in root |

**Two counts in the issue were wrong and are corrected here from the real
tree.** There are **eight** run directories, not six or seven: the eighth was
committed with raw output and no `manifest.json` at all, so no prior
measurement counted it. And there are **thirteen** `.md` attachments, not
eleven. Zero of the thirteen was referenced from any manifest. The issue's
own 9-key table is restated above against the README's real ten-key minimum,
which is why each row reads one higher.

**All eight records fail `eval-run.schema.json`, and cannot be made to pass
it without fabrication.** Measured directly:

```
runner       missing in 8/8   (these runs drove claude -p; no version string recorded)
gate         missing in 8/8   (measurement/audit sweeps, not KEEP/REJECT gate runs)
score_files  missing in 8/8
commit       missing in 2/8
```

Neither `runner` nor `gate` is recoverable, and this issue forbids
reconstructing a value by inference. `eval-run.schema.json`'s own description
draws the same line from the other side: *"a repository migrating
pre-existing records onto this contract is doing its own work, not being
retro-graded by this file."*

So the gate validates in **two layers**. Layer 1 is this repository's own
structural rules, applied to every record with no exemption. Layer 2 is the
two skill-owned schemas, applied to a record that declares itself a gate run.
Each record declares which contract it is under, and the declaration is
mandatory -- a record declaring neither value **fails**, so the exemption
cannot be reached by omission the way `models` and `commit` were omitted
before.

Nor by declaration. Blocking omission alone would have been a fail-open
dressed as a fail-closed, and the adversarial review below proved it: a
2027-dated run declaring `pre-contract` reported clean, so any future run could
skip layer 2 by writing one word plus one disclosure line -- *easier* than the
omission the declaration requirement blocks. The exemption is now pinned to the
frozen set of the eight run directories that predate the contract, with a test
asserting that set equals the committed `pre-contract` records in both
directions. It can shrink; it must not grow.

Verification commands and their output:

```
$ uv run --frozen python3 .github/scripts/gitapex_scan_eval_results_schema.py
No eval results schema drift found.

$ uv run --frozen pytest -q
3724 passed

$ uv run --frozen pytest tests/test_gitapex_scan_eval_results_schema.py \
    --cov=.github/scripts/gitapex_scan_eval_results_schema.py
139 passed
.github/scripts/gitapex_scan_eval_results_schema.py  241  0  106  0  100%

$ uv run --frozen python3 .github/scripts/gitapex_gate_evals_scripts_coverage.py \
    --coverage-json coverage.json
PASS: all 68 file(s) meet the 90.0% minimum

$ uv run --frozen python3 .github/scripts/gitapex_gate_local_preflight.py
local preflight: all 20 wired gate(s) passed.

$ uv run --frozen ruff check .            All checks passed!
$ uv run --frozen mypy --config-file pyproject.toml ...   no issues found in 159 source files
$ uv run --frozen xenon --max-absolute E --max-modules B --max-average A ...  (clean)
$ uv run --frozen python3 .github/scripts/gitapex_gate_hidden_characters.py
OK: 902 tracked file(s) carry no hidden characters.
```

Before migrating, the scanner reported at least one finding on **every one of
the eight** pre-fix records. The seven pre-fix manifest shapes are
reconstructed as fixtures in the test file, and one test asserts they
collectively fire every layer-1 rule -- so the gate is proved to fail the tree
that motivated it, not only to pass the fixed one.

A key-by-key comparison against the pre-migration tree shows **no original
value dropped or altered** in any of the seven pre-existing manifests.

`gitapex_gate_local_preflight.py`'s own prose-count gate caught the wired gate
count moving 19 -> 20 and those four files are updated here. That is the
harness working, not an unrelated edit.

## Assumptions

- **Speculation:** that the two-layer split is what the requester meant by
  "1 retro-fix". The literal reading -- all records validating against
  `eval-run.schema.json` -- is impossible without inventing `runner` and
  `gate` values, so some interpretation was unavoidable. This one was chosen
  because it is the only non-fabricating option and because the schema's own
  description explicitly disclaims retro-grading. **Fact:** the choice was
  put to the requester before implementation and confirmed.
- **Speculation:** that the manifest for the transfer-check run is complete.
  It was authored only from that run's own committed artifact plus
  `eval-status.md`'s Transfer check paragraph, both named in its
  `known_gaps`. If the run captured anything not written down in those two
  places, it is lost and this manifest cannot recover it.
- **Fact, not inference:** every recovered field cites the already-committed
  key it was read from. `#537`'s fixture set from `iterations[]` and its
  score file's `fixture_id`s; `#645-battle-test`'s trial count from
  `requested_trials`/`completed_trials`; `#646-gate2`'s model and harness
  from `run_shape` and each artifact's own header line.
- **Fact:** `#537` and `#646-gate2` record no commit. Both carry
  `commit: null` plus a `known_gaps` entry saying so, never a value derived
  from a date and an issue number.

## Risk / blast radius

Low, and the observable surface is narrow. No script, test, or workflow parses
a run manifest -- grep-confirmed before and after -- so schema-validating
these files changes no executed behaviour. What changes is (a) prose
cross-references to the moved `.md` paths, which move with them, (b) two
`.betterleaks.toml` allowlist paths, and (c) the new gate's own pass/fail,
which is new signal rather than changed behaviour.

That second item was a real defect the move introduced and it is worth naming
rather than folding into the summary: two allowlist entries pointed at
pre-move paths, and both the rename's own staged scan and the full-history
scan passed anyway -- git recorded the move as a pure rename with no added
lines, so there was nothing for the staged scan to read. Measured by
re-adding the base64 payload line as a staged edit at the new path:
`leaks found: 1` without the new entries, `no leaks found` with them. A future
edit to either fixture would have been blocked with no obvious cause. Fixed in
its own commit, with the new paths **added** rather than substituted, per
`.betterleaks.toml`'s own rule that a renamed fixture adds a name and never
replaces one.

If the gate is wrong, the failure mode is a false CI failure on a future run
record, not a corrupted one -- the scanner reads and reports, and writes
nothing. If the two skill-owned schemas are ever moved or removed, the
scanner raises rather than silently passing, so the failure is loud.

The residual risks worth naming:

- A schema pins shape, not truth. A record that misreports which model ran
  still passes. The best counter-practice in this corpus is
  `2026-08-01-issue-645-battle-test`'s own three-way
  `tester_model_requested` / `tester_model_observed` shape, which a two-key
  `models` map cannot express.
- `commit` is checked for hex shape, not for resolving on a remote,
  deliberately: a shallow clone cannot resolve a historical object name, and
  a gate failing on a property of the clone rather than of the record would
  be worse than none.
- Whether the pytest job carrying this gate is **actually** required on the
  protected branch is GitHub-side state this scanner does not read. Note this
  is narrower than the claim this template and three sibling gates make: the
  audit below found "no in-repo tooling can read it" to be false --
  `.github/rulesets/main.json` declares `pytest` required with an empty
  `bypass_actors`, and `gitapex_scan_ruleset_drift.py --scope required-checks`
  reads the live ruleset via the API on every PR. So the honest limit is
  division of labour, not unreadability. The scanner's own docstring is
  corrected; the template's copy and the three siblings' are left alone as out
  of scope.

## Rollback

A `git revert` of this PR's merge commit reverts cleanly: the scanner is a new
file, the gate row is an isolated `.gitapex/ssot.json` insertion, and the
thirteen attachment moves are recorded as renames. To disable the gate without
reverting the data migration, set the `eval-results-schema-drift` row's
`status` to `deprecated` and delete
`tests/test_gitapex_scan_eval_results_schema.py`'s
`test_real_repository_run_records_have_no_drift`; the four prose counts then
need reverting to 19 for `gitapex_gate_local_preflight.py`'s own count gate.

## Verification

Issue #926's Acceptance Criteria Map, row by row. Read this against the
issue's own stated facts rather than trusting it for being well-formed.

| Criterion | Proof method | Result |
|---|---|---|
| "results data is in scope for the reorganization too" | Scanner reports zero findings on the reworked tree and at least one on each non-compliant pre-fix manifest | **MET, exceeded.** Zero on the reworked tree; at least one on all **eight** pre-fix records, not just the four the row asks for. Registered in `.gitapex/ssot.json` as `eval-results-schema-drift`; runs in the local preflight (gate 4 of 20) |
| "store the new schema on the skill side, anticipating redistribution" | Scanner resolves both schemas under `skills/scorer-gated-skill-edits/references/` and fails loudly if either is absent | **MET.** No schema authored or modified here. Twelve tests assert the hard-error path, covering absence, a non-object schema, an invalid schema, an empty-but-legal `{}`, and the two schemas swapped for each other -- the last four were fail-open in the first version and were found by the audit |
| "1 retro-fix" (retroactive correction over forward-only) | All manifests validate; a diff review shows no field was invented | **MET, count corrected.** Eight records migrated, not six. Every recovered field cites the committed key it came from; two `commit`s are explicit nulls with disclosure |
| Missing values must not be guessed | Schema keeps `commit` required, allows `null`, requires a matching `known_gaps` entry | **MET, but not where the issue expected.** The shipped `eval-run.schema.json` permits **no** null `commit` (`pattern: ^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$`), contrary to the issue's description of it. That rule is therefore implemented in layer 1, which the issue's Non-goals allow (it authors no schema). Net effect is stricter, not looser: layer 1 accepts a null only with an anchored `^commit is null:` disclosure, and a `gate-run` record reaches the schema too and is refused one -- proved by `test_gate_run_with_a_null_commit_is_rejected_by_the_schema` |
| Attachments and their manifest must agree | Deleting a listed file fails the scanner; adding an unlisted file under `artifacts/` also fails | **MET, count corrected.** Thirteen files moved, not eleven. Both directions tested, plus traversal, absolute-path, symlink, duplicate-entry, over-long-path and path-normalization cases. `artifacts[]` covers score files too, so one reachability list governs the whole directory rather than `.md` files alone |
| Each fact has one home | No score value appears in any `artifacts/` file; every run's manifest carries `models` | **PARTIALLY MET -- see below.** Second half fully met: all eight manifests now carry `models`. First half **not** met and deliberately not attempted |

### The one criterion not met, stated plainly

"No score value appears in any `artifacts/` file" is **not** satisfied:
11 of the 13 moved files still record their own per-trial scores inline
(e.g. `### Trial 1, with-skill (score: 1.000000)`).

Those files are verbatim captures of what a run produced, and
`results/README.md`'s own convention is that a run record is "never
overwritten -- each run is a permanent, dated record." Editing eleven
historical capture files to delete numbers they recorded at capture time
would be rewriting a permanent record to satisfy a rule written afterwards,
which is a worse outcome than the duplication. What *is* fixed is the part
that actually caused drift: the manifest is now the single authoritative
machine-readable home for every score and every provenance field, and no
manifest depends on an `artifacts/` file for a fact any more
(`#645-behavioral-eval` previously recorded its model only in its `.md` files;
it now carries `models`).

The scanner therefore does **not** enforce "no score in `artifacts/`", and
that absence is disclosed here rather than left for a reader to discover. A
future run authored under this contract has no reason to duplicate, since the
Procedure and the README both point at the manifest -- but nothing mechanical
stops it.

## Skill audit evidence

- `checker-script-adversarial-review`: RAN
- `deterministic-gate-quality`: RAN

Both rounds ran in fresh isolated subagent dispatches, each given only the
target paths and told to exclude `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`, since the session
that authored the scanner is not a neutral grader of it.

**`evaluating-deterministic-gate-quality`** returned **`not well formed`**
(placement correct: mechanism-fit `repository-authored-gate`, Domain 3 primary
with Domain 1 as the earlier layer). Ten defects, live-tested against the real
corpus rather than read off the source.

**Adversarial review of the scanner and its tests** returned eleven confirmed
defects plus eight tests passing for the wrong reason, verified by mutation
testing (mirror the repo, mutate only the scanner, re-run: 19 of 21
behavioural mutants died, and the survivors are named).

Every finding was independently reproduced here before being fixed and
re-probed after. All are closed in `7274f10`; that commit message enumerates
them. The severe ones were genuine fail-opens the first version's own
docstring claimed to prevent:

| Finding | Was | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `_load_schema` guarded absence only | `{}` schema -> whole of layer 2 silently passes on the real corpus; `[]`/`null` -> uncaught `AttributeError` | four-part guard; identity swap also caught |
| `pre-contract` was self-service | a 2027-dated run declaring it reported clean | pinned to the frozen eight-record set |
| `score_files[].file` unguarded | arbitrary JSON read, values echoed into a public CI log | shares `artifacts[]`' containment predicate |
| disclosure checks were substrings | already vacuous on all 3 real null-commit records | anchored patterns |
| misplaced `results/` dirs | invisible to the gate, floor cleared anyway | new `results-dir-placement` sweep |
| symlinks | symlinked `artifacts/` disabled the orphan check entirely | new `no-symlinks` rule |
| 3 factually wrong disclosures | incl. "no in-repo tooling can read" required-check status | corrected |
| 3 tests parametrized over the constant under test | deleting a key from `README_MINIMUM_KEYS` kept the suite green | literal lists + a README-parsing equality test |

Tests went 106 -> 139; the scanner is at 100% line and branch coverage.

**Disclosed gaps in the audits themselves**, reported by the auditors rather
than by me:

- Harness-level isolation could not be verified from inside either dispatch,
  the same gap this repository's own `evaluating-deterministic-gate-quality`
  Lifecycle note discloses against itself. The coverage attestation is
  therefore scoped to this gate's own policy, not a repository-wide invariant
  sweep.
- Install-time integrity of the skills and the target is unverified in both
  directions -- no checksum or signed-release path was available. A
  non-ASCII/base64 scan of the scanner and both schemas came back clean, which
  is evidence against visible tampering, not provenance.
- Platform configuration state is unread, so dimension 23(b)/(c) and the
  non-bypassability of the deny path are `cannot determine`.
- Dimension 21 (precision audited against real firings) is structurally
  unanswerable: the gate has never fired on real traffic.
- Not fixed, and left as the auditor's own recommendation for a follow-up
  issue: a meta-gate asserting that each `policy_sources` row's declared
  authority is actually enforced by the gate citing it. Three of the findings
  above were that one shape.

### A third review round found three factual errors in this PR's own text

CodeRabbit posted 11 findings after the two audits above. Nine are fixed in
`6267035`; two are declined with reasons in a PR comment. Recorded here rather
than only in that comment, because it bears on how much weight to give the rest
of this brief: three of the nine were **statements this PR authored that were
simply untrue**, and neither audit round caught them.

1. `results/README.md` asserted that `artifacts/` "carries no score or
   provenance value of its own" and that each fact has exactly one home. Both
   false while eleven of the thirteen moved captures carry inline scores --
   which this PR's own Verification section above already admitted. A
   governance document claiming a property the tree does not have is worse than
   the duplication it was describing. Rewritten to what is true and enforced:
   `manifest.json` is authoritative for every machine-readable value; a capture
   may repeat one and those repetitions are non-authoritative.
2. The transfer-check manifest stated "every prior gate for this skill
   (battle-test x2, behavioral) used claude-fable-5". The issue #646 behavioral
   gate used `claude-sonnet-5`, as its own manifest records. The sentence was
   copied from the raw artifact, which is wrong about it; the artifact stays
   verbatim and the manifest now carries the correction.
3. That record's headline implied the behavioral result transferred. The
   spot-check delta is **-0.25** (0.75 vs 1.0), not ~0.000. Now separates the
   content-level battle-test PASS from the model-aware `INDETERMINATE` transfer
   status that follows from `models` being a self-report, both recorded as gaps.

The other six: a `#537` pointer this PR's own rename made dangle, an MD018
line-break, a test comment citing a nonexistent test name, two pre-fix shape
labels corrected by adding the missing fixture filenames (they are the
regression proof for the measured corpus, so they should match it), a
checker-report class for `dispatch-trace-check.json` in the declared root
layout, and how to read `models` in a pre-contract record.

Declined: registering `_gitapex_schema_validation.py` across five pre-existing
scanners (real, but another issue's change surface), and four findings inside
the historical captures themselves -- editing those would rewrite a permanent
record, which is the same thing item 1 above stops claiming was done.

On the two pre-merge warnings: the Linked Issues one is correct and is the ACM
row 6 gap already documented above; its suggested resolution is exactly what is
declined. The docstring-coverage one is real but misattributed -- the scanner is
at 90.9% (20 of 22 defs, module docstring present); the 7.50% is the test file,
where this repository's convention is a self-describing test name plus an inline
comment, as its sibling suites also do.

## CI status

`eval-gate` is red, and it is **not** this diff. It fails at its own
`Preflight -- require executor endpoint secrets` step because the repository
secrets `COPILOT_BASE_URL` / `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL` are unprovisioned --
the issuance path is issue #124, and the workflow's own error text already says
"this job is not yet a required status check -- see issue #582". Issue #932
recorded the same gap ("no offline check can confirm dispatchability while
COPILOT_BASE_URL / COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL are unprovisioned").

Measured rather than assumed: on runs where `eval-gate` reports success, its
`Determine touched skills` step found no `evals/` change and every subsequent
step was **skipped** -- verified on `claude/gitapex-pr-920-5hvpou` (run
31330642200: Install Nix, Preflight and the suite run all `skipped`). Every PR
that actually touches an `evals/` path -- including PR #848 and PR #949 in the
same window -- fails at that same preflight. This PR touches
`evals/*/results/`, so the diff step found changes and the preflight fired.

Nothing in this branch can fix it: provisioning a repository secret is an owner
action under Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions. No eval suite is
re-run by this issue in any case (a stated constraint), so this gate has nothing
to grade here even once the secret exists. Flagged for the owner rather than
worked around.

Every other check is green on `6267035`: pytest, mypy, ruff, actionlint,
hidden-characters, provenance-disclosure, skill-audit-disclosure,
exception-handler-gaps, plugin-root-brace-notation, ruleset-scan,
codecov/project, codecov/patch. Every gate this change is actually responsible
for passes locally -- see the Facts section.

Closes #926
Refs #932

items.title: frontend: real upload/results/reports flow, deployable compose
items.body:
Auth wiring was fundamentally broken and would have made the whole app unusable the moment AUTH_ENABLED=True (now the backend default):
- api.client.ts never attached the Authorization header to any request — every API call would 401. Added a request interceptor reading the grademind_auth cookie, and a 401 response interceptor that clears stale cookies and redirects to /login.
- store/auth-context.tsx's AuthProvider was entirely fake: hardcoded isAuthenticated: true and a hardcoded demo user, used by every authenticated page via dashboard-layout.tsx. Replaced with a real provider backed by AuthService.getCurrentSession().
- login/page.tsx was a redirect straight to /dashboard — no form existed at all. Built a real login/register form.
- middleware.ts had no auth check whatsoever. Now redirects unauthenticated requests to protected routes to /login (and signed-in users away from /login), based on the auth cookie.
- Removed the DEMO_MODE bypass (config/demo.ts, and the hasDemoSession branches throughout auth.service.ts) — this is the demo-mode leftover the task asked to remove; every one of the above bugs traces back to routes/pages built to work under that bypass and never re-verified with it off.

Upload page: added real image/PDF thumbnail previews (previously only the filename was shown) for both the exam-config documents and each student sheet in the batch list.

Results page: question breakdown now renders concept coverage (bar + %), confidence (badge), and matched/missing concept chips per question — all from fields the API already returns (QuestionEvaluation.concept_coverage/matched_keywords/missing_concepts) that the page simply wasn't displaying yet. No mock data anywhere on this page; it was already backend-fed.

Bug found via manual end-to-end verification (see below), not code review: evaluation/page.tsx's status-polling useEffect listed its own `submissions` state as a dependency, so every setSubmissions call re-triggered the effect, which fired an extra fetch and rescheduled the 2s interval — a request storm bad enough to visibly starve the actual background OCR/evaluation task of CPU/IO in the same process (measured: ~9500 requests in under 2 minutes instead of ~60). Fixed by reading current submissions through a ref instead of the dependency array.

Also found via the same manual run: autonomous evaluation derives per-question max marks from the (OCR'd) question paper, which can legitimately differ from the exam's nominal total_marks — in this run, TrOCR misread a handwritten "[20 Marks]" as "(120 Marks)". The score itself (106/120) was correct for what was actually evaluated, but submission_service.py's trigger_evaluation() never updated submission.total_marks to match, so every list view (dashboard, reports) displayed "106 / 20" — a score exceeding its stated max. Fixed by syncing total_marks from evaluation_result["max_possible"]; covered by a new regression test.

Docker/compose (verified by static review + running backend/frontend directly, since Docker itself is not available in this environment — see report):
- backend/Dockerfile now runs `alembic upgrade head` before starting uvicorn. Without this, a fresh `docker compose up` against Postgres would start the API against a database with zero tables — nothing in the stack ever ran migrations.
- docker-compose.yml: added a Postgres healthcheck and made backend's depends_on wait for it (service_healthy), and added a backend healthcheck (hits GET /) that frontend's depends_on now waits on — previously depends_on only waited for container start, a startup race.

Root README.md (new — none existed before): real Docker Compose and manual dev run steps, matching the actual current setup.

Verified manually end-to-end (backend + frontend dev servers, real browser session, since Docker isn't available here): registered a teacher account, logged in, created an exam, uploaded a question paper image, uploaded a student answer sheet, watched it process through real OCR (TrOCR — the only engine installed in this environment) and autonomous evaluation, viewed the results page with concept coverage/confidence/matched concepts, and downloaded a real 5-page generated PDF report. No mock data at any point.

Verify: backend 120 passed (unchanged), AI 167 passed / 6 skipped (unchanged, no AI/ files touched), frontend `npm run build` succeeds (type-checks + builds all 10 routes).

items.title: Fix evaluation-method bugs found in the rust_core audit
items.body:
## Summary

A full audit of the evaluation methods in `rust_core` (theory correctness vs. literature, speed, robustness) confirmed a set of bugs and gaps. This PR fixes everything the audit classified as a confirmed bug, theory deviation, or major speed/robustness issue. Lower-priority items the audit rated minor were deliberately left out.

### Correctness fixes

- **Hypervolume used only the first two objectives for m>=3** — now computed in full dimensionality, and the m>=3 path was replaced with the **WFG algorithm** (While et al. 2012) with the old recursive-slicing implementation kept as a test-only reference (property-tested against it on random fronts). The automatic reference point is now scale-invariant (`nadir + 0.1*range` instead of a constant `+1.0` term).
- **CMA-ES step-size damping** was missing the `-1` inside `d_sigma = 1 + 2*max(0, sqrt((mu_eff-1)/(n+1)) - 1) + c_sigma`, over-damping sigma adaptation. Its per-generation Jacobi eigendecomposition was also replaced with **faer's self-adjoint eigensolver** (existing dependency).
- **Entropy weighting** gave maximum weight to constant negative columns (e_j = 0 instead of 1).
- **Improvement rate** was hard-coded for minimization; it now takes the study direction, and the convergence card in the app is finally wired to real data (it was dead code).
- **All MCDM methods let +/-Inf through** the NaN filter, poisoning TOPSIS/VIKOR/PROMETHEE scores; filtering is now `is_finite()`.

### Method completeness

- **"RF-ANOVA" was actually single-shuffle permutation importance.** It is now a true Hutter et al. (2014) fANOVA: a pure-Rust CART regression forest whose leaf boxes are exactly marginalized under a uniform prior over observed ranges (main-effect variance V_j / V per tree, averaged, normalized), with an analytically hand-verified decomposition test. n_trees=64 matches Optuna's fanova default.
- **VIKOR** now implements the Opricovic & Tzeng (2004) compromise acceptance conditions C1/C2 with DQ = 1/(J-1), returns the compromise set, and defensively normalizes weights. The MCDM scatter widget lists the compromise set and marks members in the detail modal.
- **Ridge sensitivity** now filters NaN/Inf rows (previously one bad cell poisoned every beta via the Cholesky solve) and reports 80/20 **holdout R2**, unified with the tree metrics so the R2 badges in the UI are comparable. The generic in-sample Ridge primitives used by PDP/Sobol/surrogates are unchanged.

### Performance / robustness

- **PROMETHEE** no longer materializes the O(n^2) preference matrix (~20 GB at 50k trials); flows are computed streaming in O(n) memory with rayon, bit-identical to the old results.
- Spearman applies pairwise deletion for non-finite values, Sobol guards `n_samples == 0`, and the LightGBM FFI boundary asserts the C API's length contract.

### Docs

- `theory/{ja,en}` updated or added to match the implementations: fANOVA, hypervolume/WFG (new page), VIKOR C1/C2 (also fixing a swapped condition description in the ja doc), Ridge holdout evaluation, k-means init strategies, entropy edge cases.

## Test plan

- `cargo test --workspace` — 609 (core) + 688 (desktop) passing, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` for both crates — clean
- New tests include hand-computed analytic values for fANOVA and hypervolume, a WFG-vs-slicing property test, VIKOR C1/C2 case tests, Ridge NaN/Inf/determinism tests, PROMETHEE 10k performance test, and direction-aware convergence tests.

items.title: docs(solutions): record the mog-sdk calculated-column import defect
items.body:
## Summary

A delivered 4,167-row client workbook opens in the canvas and renders `#CALC!` across its entire Weekly Summary grid, while the file on disk carries correct cached values throughout. The grid looks finished and the Save button is live next to it — pressing Save would write `#CALC!` into the client's file. This PR documents the defect; it changes no code.

The cause is upstream. `@mog-sdk/sdk` 0.10.5 mis-evaluates some XLSX table calculated columns on import and then marks the dependency graph clean. `recalculateAll()` returns in **0 ms** and changes nothing: the wrong values are settled, not pending. Nothing in the canvas reports an error, because as far as the engine is concerned there isn't one.

Which columns fail is the part worth reading:

| Column | Formula shape | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Direction` | references a static column only | correct on all 4,167 rows |
| `DefaultCategory` | `IF(... XLOOKUP(...))` | `#CALC!` on 8 rows |
| `EffectiveCategory` | `[#This Row]` ref to another calculated column | `#CALC!` on all 4,167 |
| `UniqueTxnKey` | range built with `:` over structured refs | `#VALUE!` on all 4,167 |

`Direction` succeeding rules out calculated columns as a category. And this is not error propagation: `DefaultCategory` is correct on 4,159 rows while `EffectiveCategory` fails on all 4,167 — the consumer fails where the producer succeeded. The 8 `DefaultCategory` failures are position-dependent rather than value-dependent, clustering in two narrow row bands on inputs the same column computes correctly 19 to 486 times elsewhere.

Seven hypotheses were tested and disproven, including the one that had already been written down as the diagnosis — "Mog can't evaluate SUMIFS against structured table references" — which is false and had been sending readers the wrong way.

## What the doc recommends

Two things, neither of them applied here. Upstream, file this as a **wrong-result evaluation bug**, separately from the ~104 s single-threaded import; filing them together invites a scheduling fix for a correctness defect. In this repo, add an open-time guard that compares the engine's computed values against the cached `<v>` results the workbook already carries, surfaces any mismatch through the Adapter Probe reason, and disables Save.

That guard is deliberately shaped around the failure mode rather than the symptom. Every disproven mitigation assumed the engine would signal something — an error, a pending calculation, a budget to raise. The 0 ms recalculation proves it won't.

## New concepts

**Value fidelity — and using a file's own cached results as an independent oracle.**

Durability and identity are the properties this repo already enforces on saves: bytes land whole, and the revision matches what the session opened. Value fidelity is a third and separate property — whether the values being written are the ones the workbook's formulas actually produce. A save can be non-torn, fully flushed, and revision-clean while carrying values the engine got wrong.

It earns a name here because the existing verification cannot see it. The save path already reopens the written file with the headless engine and reads it back before trusting it — but a value the engine got wrong on import survives that round trip intact, because the engine agrees with itself. A same-engine round trip measures durability, never fidelity.

The way out is that Excel ships its own answer key: it writes a cached `<v>` alongside every formula it evaluates. That is a cheap, local, high-signal oracle. At open time, before any user edit, any disagreement between the engine and the cached value can only be an import defect.

```xml
<!-- Excel's cached result for Q2 is "Subcontractors"; Mog computes #CALC! -->
<c r="Q2" t="str"><f>IF(TxnLog[[#This Row],[CategoryOverride]]<>"",...)</f><v>Subcontractors</v></c>
```

The generalizable form: when a system reports a settled value, verify it against a record produced outside that system. "It returned without erroring" is not evidence. The boundary is that the oracle only holds while it is independent — once the user edits a cell, the cached value is stale by design and the comparison must stop.

## Validation

No code changed, so there is no behavior to exercise. The repo's two documentation validators pass: frontmatter is well-formed, and the claim checker resolved 4 file paths and 11 links with 0 flags.

The measurements in the doc come from headless runs against the real workbook — the per-column error counts, the 0 ms `recalculateAll()`, the 8 position-dependent failures, and the import timings for both lanes (104 s browser, 77-91 s headless). The `openpyxl` minimal repro is recorded as *not* reproducing: the defect is size- and mix-dependent, which is data about the bug rather than grounds to dismiss it.

items.title: Game plo
items.body:
Adds PLO (4-card Omaha Hi) as a third game type and consolidates the per-game simulators into a single shared engine.

## New game: PLO
- New `plo` game type end to end: sim engine, game selector, settings page, API schema, and localStorage cache.
- Reuses the Omaha "exactly 2 hole cards + 3 board cards" rule from Big O, but high-only (no 8-or-better low pot).

## Sim refactor
- Replaces the separate `simulation.ts` (Big O) and `holdem.ts` simulators with one Monte Carlo engine (`sim/engine.ts`) parameterized by per-game showdown rules (`sim/games.ts`): hole-card usage (Omaha's exactly-2 vs Hold'em's best-of-seven) and whether a Hi-Lo low pot is contested.
- `simulate()` is overloaded on game type so callers get `HiLoResult` for Big O and `HighOnlyResult` for Hold'em/PLO.
- Hand evaluation now uses a single `scoreFiveCardHand` with full kicker resolution for all games, replacing the old kicker-less Hi-Lo scorer. Fixes two evaluation bugs: score-band overflow that ranked a full house over quads, and ignored kickers causing false splits.
- Results UI split into `HighResults` (Hold'em/PLO) and `BigOResults` (Hi-Lo breakdown with scoop/low tallies).

## Other
- New default Big O hands and board.
- Engine tests cover all three games: tally invariants, seeded reproducibility, exact full-board cases, and regression tests for the evaluation fixes.

items.title: fix(ci): grant pull-requests:write in dbt-deploy.yml/dbt-scheduled.yml
items.body:
Closes #24. Root cause of #21.

## Purpose
`dbt Deploy` and `dbt Scheduled` have hit `startup_failure` (0 jobs run) across two prior fix attempts (#22, #23), both of which targeted a hypothesized `inputs.*` cross-context evaluation bug. Neither fix worked, including on `workflow_dispatch` where that hypothesis predicted success — proving it wrong.

## Root cause (actually found this time)
The Actions REST API doesn't surface the validation error for `startup_failure` — it's only rendered in the run page HTML banner:

```
Invalid workflow file: dbt-deploy.yml (Line: 34, Col: 3): Error calling workflow
'.../dbt-run.yml@<sha>'. The workflow is requesting 'pull-requests: write',
but is only allowed 'pull-requests: none'.
```

`dbt-run.yml` declares `pull-requests: write` at its own top level (used by its PR-comment step). A reusable workflow's declared `permissions:` must be a subset of what the calling job grants, or GitHub rejects the whole run before any job starts. `dbt-ci.yml` already grants `pull-requests: write` and has always worked; `dbt-deploy.yml` and `dbt-scheduled.yml` only granted `contents: read`.

## Changes
- `dbt-deploy.yml`: add `pull-requests: write` to top-level `permissions:`; trimmed the now-incorrect comment block that attributed the failure to the `if:`/`inputs.*` split (that restructuring was harmless but not the fix).
- `dbt-scheduled.yml`: same permissions fix.

## Test evidence
- `actionlint`: zero findings.
- `yaml.safe_load`: both files parse.
- Will trigger live `workflow_dispatch` for both workflows immediately after merge and post results here before closing #21/#24.

## Security impact
None — grants the same `pull-requests: write` scope `dbt-ci.yml` already has in this repo; does not touch `contents`, secrets, or Snowflake credentials.

## Rollback
Revert this PR — `dbt Deploy`/`dbt Scheduled` go back to `startup_failure`; `dbt-ci.yml` (PR job) is unaffected either way.

items.title: fix(cel): honor failurePolicy Fail for validation eval errors
items.body:
Hey folks! I was following the active discussion on #3059 and had some cycles to explore implementing the "something like 2" direction locally. I figured I'd open up this self-contained PR with my approach in case it helps move the needle forward—feel free to use it, close it, or pull from it as needed!

Following up on the failurePolicy discussion in the issue - this implements the "something like 2" direction, narrowly.

The problem: `newVAP` was throwing away `spec.failurePolicy`, so a validation whose CEL expression errored at runtime always landed as `Skipped/Unknown` offline. But every policy we bundle is `failurePolicy: Fail`, so on a real cluster that exact object gets *denied*. The scan was ending up quieter than admission and silently losing the finding - which is precisely when you'd want it to speak up.

What I did:

- Preserve `failurePolicy` on the VAP, resolving it to `Fail` when omitted (matching the apiserver's default).
- Add a small `expressionError` wrapper + `IsExpressionError` in the `cel` package to tell apart the two kinds of errors that can land on a `ValidationResult.Err`:
  - a *runtime* eval error or a non-bool result - the expression actually ran and blew up, which is a verdict the apiserver can reach, so `failurePolicy` should govern it;
  - *offline-only* failures - compile errors (a broken bundle, which the cluster could never install), cost-budget exhaustion, and cancellation - which stay `Skipped` because the cluster never produces them.
- In `runCELOnK8s`, under `Fail` a runtime eval error now emits a failure (deny) whose message is the error text, instead of dropping into `outcome.skipped`. An explicit `Ignore` keeps the old skipped behavior - I left `Ignore` alone rather than mapping it to `pass`, which felt like a separate call.

I went with the narrow version on purpose: the offline engine evaluates the raw manifest with no schema defaulting, so some expressions can error on things admission would silently default-fill. Those errors stay "unknown" rather than being promoted to a deny, so we don't start inventing failures on perfectly fine workloads. The guarded-bundle work already in `TestNoEvalErrorOnMinimalWorkloads` keeps that class in check; the one real error we know about today (C-0020's missing `params.settings.cloudProvider`) now correctly reports as a failure to match the cluster.

Verification: `go test ./core/pkg/opaprocessor/...` is 339 passed and clean under `-race` (new tests cover the classification and the Fail/Ignore/omitted matrix plus an end-to-end eval-error-denied case through `runCELOnK8s`). Full `go test ./core/...` is 3512 passed with one pre-existing unrelated failure (`TestExcludeFilesUnderDirectories`, also fails on master). `go vet` and `gofmt` are clean.

One thing I'd flag for review: treating an eval error as a deny changes the status of objects whose expression can't be evaluated from "skipped" to "failed" when the policy is `Fail`. That's the intended direction, but it's a verdict change, so worth a second set of eyes on whether the "deny with the raw error as the message" presentation is what you want for the printers.

items.title: feat(rules)!: gate on ERC-5192, unregister erc721-min-balance
items.body:
Closes #27. Leaves #28 open by design — see below.

## Why

The gate bounds Sybils only if the gating asset cannot move, and the tree took that on trust. `erc721-min-balance` reads a bare `balanceOf` and asserts nothing about transferability, while DESIGN.md stated non-transferability as a *property of the Pass*. Neither premise held for what is deployed (a plain OpenZeppelin `ERC721`, no `_update` override, no lock — and MintPass would not have fixed it either: its cooldown is an off-chain plugin option a pinned `balanceOf` inherits nothing from).

The amplification that opens: every bundle is verified at its OWN pinned block, stays live for `voteExpiryBuckets`, and the winner set is LWW-keyed per wallet — so one token walked A → B → C inside a single expiry window backs three concurrent live votes. No forgery, no back-dating, not one invalid ballot, which is why nothing in the verify pipeline can catch it. The ceiling is the number of transfers inside one expiry window, not the number of Passes.

## What changed

**New rule `erc5192-min-balance`** (registered): the same scoring as before plus `supportsInterface(0xb45a3c0e)` at the same pinned block. A contract that does not declare ERC-5192 scores `0n` for every wallet.

- The probe is hoisted to **one read per (contract, block)** and issued *in parallel* with the balances, so the read coalescer folds it into the same `aggregate3` — no extra round trip on the coalesced path, one extra read on a raw client.
- A **reverting** probe (a contract with no ERC-165) reads as "does not declare"; a **transport** failure still throws. That split keeps a flaky gateway infra-class (gossip `ignore`, background retry) instead of turning it into a consensus `reject` that scores honest relayers down.
- The shared `balanceOf` batching (200/`aggregate3`, ≤2 in flight, per-chunk retry) moved to an internal `src/rules/nft-balance.ts` so the two rules cannot drift on the tuned numbers.

**`erc721-min-balance` unregistered**, but kept in-tree, exported and unit-tested: a host that genuinely wants a transferable gate registers it through the `rules` override map. The library stops blessing the configuration; it does not forbid it.

**`erc20-balance` stays unregistered** (#28): the ERC-5192 fix cannot transfer to a fungible balance — it can be neither soulbound nor LWW-keyed by token id — so it needs a hold-duration guard instead. #28 stays open as the standing blocker; this PR only pins the exclusion.

## Test vectors

- `src/crdt/amplification.test.ts` — one asset walked A → B → C inside one expiry window yields **three concurrent winner-set entries**, each wallet admitted by the *real* rule at its own pinned block; the fungible variant of the same; the v1 gate admitting nobody on a non-declaring contract; and the proposed hold-duration predicate (`min` at pinned **and** at `pinned − E`) collapsing the fungible case back to one vote — the failing-then-passing vector #28 asks for, ready for whoever ships the guard.
- `src/rules/rules.test.ts` — the registry's exact contents, the non-declaring contract scoring `0n` (batched and single), the single hoisted probe, revert-vs-transport classification, and both `UnknownRuleError` recusals.
- `src/verify/bundle.test.ts` — the pipeline-level `reject` for a non-declaring gate contract.

## Docs

DESIGN.md's "Does one Pass mean one vote?" is rewritten: non-transferability as a **requirement the gate rule enforces**, what `supportsInterface` does and does not prove (ERC-5192 permits unlockable tokens — the check refuses contracts that do not even claim the property), why "reject ballots not stamped at the current bucket" and token-id-keyed LWW both fail, and a **Cutover ordering** section. README, ROADMAP, AGENTS.md, `benchmark/RESULTS.md` methodology, and a note in `examples/5chan.ts` (its pinned manifest still names the old rule, so it recuses until step 4) updated to match.

## Rollout

Both halves re-CID every criteria document, and the topic is that CID, so all directory contests get new topics. One cutover, in order:

1. release this;
2. upgrade seeder + clients;
3. redeploy the Pass locked (Rinse12/testnet-5chan-pass#1) and re-mint holders;
4. only then flip the `lists` manifest to the new contract + rule name.

Step 4 before step 2 makes every un-upgraded client throw `UnknownRuleError` — correct behaviour (recuse, don't miscount), but it must not land early. Votes on the old topics are not migrated; they decay on their own expiry.

## Verification

`npm test` (411), `npm run test:integration` (10, real gossipsub + pkc-js hosts), both typechecks, `npm run build`, and `npm run bench:warm-restart` (still 0 gate reads on reload) all pass. `src/rules` is at 100% coverage.

**Outstanding:** `bench:cold-join` has not been re-run against `benchmark/RESULTS.md`. The gate now issues one extra coalesced read per (contract, sample block) on the cold-join verify path, so the comparison should happen before release.

items.title: Backtest engine: O(log n) point-in-time lookups (15-year run: 15 min → ~11 s)
items.body:
## Why: a 15-year backtest ran for 15+ minutes and still wasn't done

After the cache fixes (PRs #34/#35) the **data load** is fast, and the Render log confirmed it: `Backtest data loaded: 215/215 tickers scored; entering simulation.` The remaining time was all in the **simulation loop**, not the network.

Root cause: the day loop needs "the last row of a ticker at or before date T" in three places — portfolio valuation (`_cur_price`), exit checks, and the entry scan. All three did it as:

```python
mask = sc.index <= today_ts
row  = sc.loc[mask].iloc[-1]
```

`sc.loc[mask]` materializes a fresh copy of the ticker's **entire history-up-to-T** (all rows, all columns) — on every ticker, every trading day. That's **O(days² × tickers)**. A cProfile of a 3-year run (network stubbed, real seed cache) showed **42s of 59s** inside pandas `.loc`/`take_nd` row-copying (1.18M `_take_nd_ndarray` calls). A full 15-year run scales ~25× worse → never completes in reasonable time.

## Fix

Precompute each ticker's `Close` and `composite_score` columns as plain numpy arrays **once**, and locate the row with the index's own `searchsorted` — **O(log n)**, no per-lookup copy. (Used the `DatetimeIndex.searchsorted`, not a raw `np.searchsorted` on `.asi8`: the frames come back as `datetime64[us]`, so comparing against a nanosecond `ts.value` would silently mismatch — caught and fixed during verification.) Values are read back through the same `_safe_float`, so results are unchanged.

## Verification — byte-for-byte identical results

sha256 of the full result dict (params + summary + every trade + yearly + spy_comparison), original engine vs optimized, network stubbed against the real 2010-2026 seed cache:

| Config | Window | Hash (orig == opt) | Time orig → opt |
|---|---|---|---|
| 252d_only | 2018–2020 (2yr) | `6b0f9343` | 23.2s → **3.7s** |
| 252d_only | 2017–2020 (3yr) | `675d3bc3` | 31.5s → **3.5s** |
| TP 30 / SL 20 / trail 25 | 2017–2020 | `a2c5304a` | — |
| threshold_or_252d | 2017–2020 | `f5dac381` | — |
| close-fill (legacy same-bar) | 2017–2020 | `59efd490` | — |

items.title: Clarify auto-triage handling for human bug reports
items.body:
Auto-Triage could prioritize machine-generated report detection without explicitly directing classification of genuine human-authored bug reports. Detailed issues describing failures, expected/actual behavior, or reproductions now receive actionable triage.

- **Classification order**
  - Distinguishes generated aggregate reports from all other issues.
  - Requires both a report-style title and a generated marker/footer before applying only `report`.

- **Human bug triage**
  - Treats unexpected behavior, expected-vs-actual results, reproducible failures, and errors as `bug` reports even when the title omits “bug”.
  - Adds a matching component label when identifiable; otherwise adds `needs-triage`.

- **Workflow evaluation**
  - Adds an evaluation criterion for labeling non-report bug reports.

```text
human issue with expected/actual failure
  → bug + relevant component
  → bug + needs-triage (when component is unclear)

generated report title + generated marker/footer
  → report only
```

- Fixes #50595

items.title: fix(eval): chunk encoder batches so evaluation cannot exhaust memory
items.body:
Training now works. The last run logged a real LoRA budget:

```
LoRA parameter budget: total_parameters=23,051,136
                       trainable_parameters=337,920
                       trainable_percent=1.466
```

It still timed out — but in **evaluation**, not training, after 26 minutes on a step that should take a couple.

## The bug

Evaluation encoded 1,000 documents in a **single ONNX call, twice** — once through the base model, once through the candidate. Attention allocates `batch × heads × seq × seq`, so 1,000 documents at 256 tokens is roughly **3.1 GB in fp32** against a 3 GB container limit.

The embedding worker had always chunked at 50. This path chunked not at all.

## Fix

`encode_with_session` now chunks internally at 32. Every caller funnels through it — the worker, the serving engine, and both evaluation paths — so they're bounded together rather than each needing its own limit.

**Chunking is verified not to change results:** a document embedded alone matches its vector from a batch spanning three chunks at cosine `1.0`. That holds because pooling is attention-masked, so padding never contributes.

The evaluation set is also capped at 400 documents. Each is encoded twice, so it dominates pipeline runtime, and a few hundred across two domains already give a stable MRR.

139 passed / 7 skipped, verified against `.env.example`.
